cards.explanation: The answer is priests, friends. God says Aaron and his four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, are to serve Him as priests (Exodus 28:1). Aaron is Moses' brother, and the whole job here is serving God. I'd call that a family business.
The answer is glory and splendor. God says to make holy garments for Aaron "…to give him glory and splendor." (Exodus 28:2). These aren't just work clothes, friends. They're meant to look the part.

The answer is the skilled craftsmen, friends. God tells Moses, "You are to instruct all the skilled craftsmen, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, to make garments for Aaron’s consecration…" (Exodus 28:3). So Moses is told to instruct the craftsmen, and the garment-making goes to them. Good news for everybody who has watched me try to thread a needle with a mustache.

The answer is False. The text says they make these holy garments "…for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they may serve Me as priests." (Exodus 28:4). So Aaron isn't the only one getting dressed up, friends. His sons are in the wardrobe plan too.

The answer is the sons of Israel, bakers! God says to take two onyx stones and engrave on them "…the names of the sons of Israel…" (Exodus 28:9). Six names go on one stone and six on the other (Exodus 28:10). That's a lot of names on a small stone. I can barely fit a cookie on my stamp, so I'm impressed.
The answer is birth. Six names go on one stone and six on the other, "…in the order of their birth." (Exodus 28:10). Oldest to youngest, no cutting in line. Everybody gets their spot.

The answer is False. The stones are fastened "…on the shoulder pieces of the ephod…" (Exodus 28:12). Aaron's turban is a different piece, and what goes on the front of it is a gold plate (Exodus 28:36-37). So these stones sit on his shoulders, friends.

The answer is memorial, bakers. God says, "Aaron is to bear their names on his two shoulders as a memorial before the LORD." (Exodus 28:12). The stones are fastened on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Twelve names on two shoulders. I bet that feels like carrying a full tray of cookies.

The answer is True, friends. God says to make the breastpiece "…with the same workmanship as the ephod." and to build it with gold, blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and fine linen (Exodus 28:15). It matches the ephod. Same fine work, same materials.

The answer is square. The breastpiece "…must be square when folded over double, a span long and a span wide." (Exodus 28:16). Four equal sides, nothing fancy, friends. Even my cookie cutters would be proud.
The answer is one tribe's name, bakers. The twelve stones are "…each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 28:21). One stone, one tribe. Nobody gets left out.

The answer is over his heart, friends. God says that in the Holy Place Aaron "…shall bear the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of judgment…" (Exodus 28:29). That's a pretty close place to keep people. I think that says something.

The answer is False. The text says Aaron bears the names "…as a continual reminder before the LORD." whenever he enters the Holy Place (Exodus 28:29). It's not a first-day thing, friends. It keeps going.

The answer is over his heart. God says to place the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece "…so that they will also be over Aaron’s heart whenever he comes before the LORD." (Exodus 28:30). They ride in the same spot as the names, friends. Same place, same breastpiece.

The answer is judgment, bakers. "Aaron will continually carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD." (Exodus 28:30). It's the same word as in the breastpiece's name. Continually means he carries it every time.

The answer is gold bells. Ding, ding, friends. God says to make pomegranates of yarn all the way around the lower hem, "…with gold bells between them…" (Exodus 28:33). Pomegranate, bell, pomegranate, bell. That's a hem with a rhythm.

The answer is sanctuary, bakers. God says, "…its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD…" (Exodus 28:35). Around the lower hem, gold bells alternate with pomegranates (Exodus 28:33, 34). So that sound goes with Aaron every time he walks in or out.

The answer is True, friends. God says Aaron must wear the robe whenever he ministers, and its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary, "…so that he will not die." (Exodus 28:35). That's a serious line, and I'd say it's worth a quiet moment. God means these instructions to be followed.

The answer is HOLY TO THE LORD, bakers. God tells Moses to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it "…as on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 28:36). A blue cord mounts it on the front of the turban (Exodus 28:37). It's worn on Aaron's forehead (Exodus 28:38).

The answer is True, bakers. God says, "Fasten to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban." (Exodus 28:37). Gold plate, blue cord, front of the turban. That's a very well-dressed turban.

The answer is so they may be acceptable before the LORD. The plate "…shall always be on his forehead, so that they may be acceptable before the LORD." (Exodus 28:38). It's tied to the holy gifts the Israelites consecrate, friends. Aaron wears it for them.

The answer is True, friends. God says, "Make tunics, sashes, and headbands for Aaron’s sons, to give them glory and splendor." (Exodus 28:40). Those are the same words He used for Aaron's garments (Exodus 28:2). The sons get the glory and splendor too.

The answer is anoint and consecrate them. After Moses puts the garments on, God says to "…anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them so that they may serve Me as priests." (Exodus 28:41). The clothes come first, then the setting apart, friends. Both are part of the plan.
The answer is permanent, bakers. God says, "This is to be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants." (Exodus 28:43). It isn't a one-time thing. It keeps going down the family line.
